exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Choosing the Rescue Team
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: We must choose two more sailors for the rescue boat. Who do you suggest?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: I think we need Frank Worsley. He is an excellent navigator.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: A good navigator is the most important thing for such a journey.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Yes. Without him, we could easily lose our way on the rough sea.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: What about Tom Crean? He is strong, brave, and full of energy.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Perfect. We will need his strength to row for days without rest.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Then it is settled. Worsley to guide us, and Crean for his power.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Let's tell the captain. The sooner we set off, the better.

exercises.translation_cn: 两人为救援船挑选另外两名水手:B 推荐沃斯利,因为他是出色的领航员;A 说领航员对这样的航行最重要;还选了汤姆·克林,因为他强壮勇敢、精力充沛,需要他的力气连日划船;两人决定告诉船长,越早出发越好。

questions.stem: What are the two speakers trying to do?
options: Choose sailors for the rescue boat.

questions.stem: Why do they want Frank Worsley?
Why is a navigator so important for the journey?
options: So they will not lose their way on the rough sea.

questions.stem: Why do they choose Tom Crean?
options: Because he is quiet and shy.
Because they need his strength to row for days.
Because he is good at advertising.

questions.stem: What do they decide to do next?
options: Tell the captain and set off soon.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 What Courage Really Means
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many people believe that brave heroes never feel afraid.
In truth, courage is not the absence of fear.
It is the choice to act well even while you are afraid.
Real courage often shows itself in small, quiet actions.
Anyone can learn to be braver, one step at a time.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多人认为勇敢的英雄从不害怕;其实勇气并非没有恐惧,而是在害怕时仍选择做正确的事;真正的勇气常常体现在微小而安静的行动中;任何人都能一步一步学会更勇敢。

questions.stem: What do many people wrongly believe about heroes?
According to the passage, what is courage?
Where does real courage often show itself?
What does the passage say about becoming braver?
options: Anyone can learn it step by step.

questions.stem: What is the main message of the passage?

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Interview with a Climber
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: You climbed the mountain after losing your sight. Wasn't that frightening?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Of course it was. But I refused to let blindness end the life I loved.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: How did you find your way up without being able to see?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: I felt every hold with my hands and listened to my friends' voices.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: That must have taken years of practice and patience.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: It did. I trained my body to trust touch and sound instead of sight.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: What would you say to young people who face hard problems?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: The biggest mountains we climb are often the ones inside our minds.

exercises.translation_cn: 记者采访一位失明后仍登山的攀登者:他承认害怕,但拒绝让失明终结自己热爱的生活;他靠双手感觉每个抓握点、靠朋友的声音找路;这需要多年练习,让身体学会信任触觉和听觉;他对面对困难的年轻人说:我们攀登的最大的山,往往在自己心里。

questions.stem: What difficulty did the climber face?
How did he find his way up the mountain?
options: By feeling holds and listening to friends.

questions.stem: What did the years of training teach his body to do?
options: To need no rest at all.
To trust touch and sound instead of sight.

questions.stem: What does he tell young people who face hard problems?
options: The biggest mountains are inside our minds.

questions.stem: How did the climber feel about the climb?
options: It was frightening, but he refused to give up.
He felt no fear at all.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 The Power of One Small Step
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: When a problem feels too big, it can stop us before we even begin.
The secret is to break it into small, simple steps.
Do not ask how to finish everything at once.
Just ask what you can do in the next hour.
Many small steps, taken with hope, can carry you a very long way.
exercises.translation_cn: 当问题显得太大时,它会在我们开始之前就让我们停步;秘诀是把它拆成小而简单的步骤;别问如何一次完成全部,只问下一个小时你能做什么;许多带着希望迈出的小步,能把你带到很远的地方。

questions.stem: What can a problem that feels too big do to us?
What is the secret the speaker gives?
options: To ask others to do it.
To break it into small steps.

questions.stem: What should we NOT ask, according to the passage?
options: How to finish everything at once.

questions.stem: What should we ask instead?
options: What we can do in the next hour.

questions.stem: What can many small steps do?
options: Carry you a very long way.

exercises.title: U4 听力·对话 Getting Ready for the Expedition
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: The expedition leaves next month. Have you been preparing for it?

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: Yes, I've been training every single day to build up my endurance.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Good. The cold and the long marches will test all of us.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: I know. I've also been reading about how others survived such journeys.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: That's wise. Their stories can teach us how to handle real danger.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: What worries me most is the rough sea on the way there.

transcript.speaker: A
transcript.text: Stay calm and trust the team. Together we can face anything.

transcript.speaker: B
transcript.text: You're right. With good preparation and courage, we'll be fine.

exercises.translation_cn: 两人谈下个月出发的远征:B 说每天训练以增强耐力;A 说严寒和长途行军会考验大家;B 还读了别人如何在这种旅程中生存;A 说这些故事能教人应对真正的危险;B 最担心途中汹涌的海;A 让他保持冷静、信任团队;B 同意,有充分准备和勇气就没问题。

questions.stem: When does the expedition leave?
How has B been preparing?
options: By training every day to build endurance.

questions.stem: Why has B been reading about other journeys?
options: To learn how others survived such trips.
Because there is nothing else to do.

questions.stem: What worries B the most?
options: The rough sea on the way there.

questions.stem: What advice does A give B?
options: Stay calm and trust the team.

exercises.title: U4 听力·短文 A Word for Hard Times
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: If you are going through a hard time, please remember that you are not alone.
Almost everyone meets adversity at some point in life.
Do not be afraid to ask a friend or teacher for help.
A worry that is shared with someone always feels lighter.
This difficult time is only one chapter in your long story.
exercises.translation_cn: 如果你正经历艰难时光,请记住你并不孤单;几乎每个人在人生某个阶段都会遭遇逆境;不要害怕向朋友或老师求助;与人分担的忧虑总会轻一些;这段艰难只是你漫长故事中的一个篇章。

questions.stem: What does the speaker want listeners in hard times to remember?
options: That they should hide their feelings.

questions.stem: According to the passage, who meets adversity?
What does the speaker say about asking for help?
options: Do not be afraid to ask a friend or teacher.

questions.stem: Why is a shared worry better?
How does the speaker describe this difficult time?
options: As something to be ashamed of.
As only one chapter in a long story.
